grammar_focus: be likely / be able + to do、倍数表达(160 times more distant than / twice as tall as / a sixth of)、it takes + (精力/时间)+ to do、比较级 less/more … than、不定式作目的状语(To escape …, one must …)(NCE4 无 KS 页,考点由课文结构自取;IP:源为《7 Days》一篇论‘月球成太阳系工业枢纽、移民火星’的文章,内含真实人物阿瑟·C·克拉克的‘革命性想法三阶段’——已泛化为‘一位著名科幻作家’,通用天文/航天事实用 100% 原创行文复述;题材=太空科普·无害;美语化 colonize/program;第四册第35课)
scene: 月球很可能成为太阳系的工业枢纽:它可用从月岩里轻易提取的氧,为往来飞船供给燃料。原因在于它的引力。由于月球的质量只有地球的约十八分之一,从月球出发、飞越二十五万英里进入地球轨道,所需能量竟比从地球表面爬升区区两百英里还要少——少约百分之九十七。这听来匪夷所思,却极易算出。要靠火箭挣脱地球,你得达到每秒约七英里的速度;而从月球出发,对应的速度只有一点五英里。由于月球表面的引力仅为地球的六分之一,把飞船加速到那个更温和的速度,所耗能量远比在地球上少。简言之,月球居民飞入太空的花费,只相当于地球同类的百分之三。一位著名的科幻作家曾说,一个革命性的想法通常要经历三个阶段:先是‘不可能——别浪费我时间’;接着是‘可能,但不值得做’;最后是‘我一直就说这是个好主意’。移民火星——一个比月球还远一百六十倍的世界——这一想法,将在相当数量的人长期定居太空之时,决然地从第二阶段迈入第三阶段。火星对那些跃跃欲试的远航者有一种非凡的吸引力。美国、俄罗斯和欧洲满是热心人,其中不乏严肃的资深科学家,他们都梦想把人送上火星。这份心愿不难理解,因为它是太阳系里最像地球的那个世界。那里有红色的沙漠——故得旧名‘红色星球’——有万里无云的天空与骤起的沙暴,有远比大峡谷宽阔的裂谷,还有至少一座高逾珠峰两倍的山。总之,它似乎几乎是理想的定居之地。

grammar_card.title: be likely/able to do / 倍数表达 / it takes … to do / 比较级 less·more…than / 目的状语 to do
grammar_card.intro: ①be likely to do(很可能);be able to do(能够)。②倍数表达:160 times more distant than;twice as tall as;a sixth of。③it takes + 精力/时间 + to do。④比较级 less/more … than。⑤不定式作目的状语:To escape from the Earth, one must …。

rows: is likely to become the hub
it takes + 精力 + to do
it takes much less energy to accelerate
To escape, one must reach a speed

specialRules.rule: 倍数放在比较结构最前面:… times + 比较级 + than;… times + as + 原级 + as。
less 修饰不可数(less energy);fewer 修饰可数(fewer ships);别混。
美式拼写:colonize(殖民,英式 colonise)、program(计划,英式 programme)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — When will it be possible for us to think seriously about colonizing Mars?
options: When a significant number of people are living permanently in space
As soon as the Moon is reached

passage: The Moon is likely to become the industrial hub of the Solar System, supplying the fuel for its ships from oxygen easily extracted from the lunar rocks. The reason lies in its gravity. Because the Moon has only about an eighteenth of the Earth's mass, it takes far less energy — some ninety-seven per cent less — to travel the quarter of a million miles from the Moon into Earth-orbit than to make the short two-hundred-mile climb from the Earth's own surface. This may sound fantastic, but it is easily worked out. To escape from the Earth in a rocket, one must reach a speed of about seven miles a second; the comparable speed from the Moon is only one and a half. Because the gravity at the Moon's surface is only a sixth of the Earth's, it takes much less energy to accelerate to that gentler speed than it does on Earth. Moon-dwellers, in short, will be able to fly out into space at only three per cent of the cost paid by their terrestrial cousins. A well-known science-fiction writer once observed that a revolutionary idea usually passes through three phases: first, 'It's impossible — don't waste my time'; then, 'It's possible, but not worth doing'; and at last, 'I said it was a good idea all along.' The idea of colonizing Mars — a world a hundred and sixty times more distant than the Moon — will move decisively from the second phase to the third when a significant number of people are living permanently in space. Mars holds an extraordinary fascination for would-be voyagers. America, Russia, and Europe are filled with enthusiasts, many of them serious and senior scientists, who dream of sending people there. Their aim is understandable, for it is the one world in the Solar System that is most like the Earth. It is a place of red sandy deserts — hence its old name, the Red Planet — of cloudless skies and sudden sandstorms, of chasms far wider than the Grand Canyon and at least one mountain more than twice as tall as Everest. It seems, in short, almost ideal for settlement.

grammar_points.name: be likely / be able + to do
倍数表达(times + 比较级 + than / as … as)
it takes + 精力/时间 + to do
不定式作目的状语(To do …)

stage5.stem: "The Moon is likely ___ become the industrial hub of space."(be likely + 不定式,‘很可能…’,填不定式符号)
stage5.stem_cn: 月球很可能成为太空的工业枢纽。

stage5.stem: "Moon-dwellers will be able ___ fly cheaply into space."(be able + 不定式,‘能够…’,填不定式符号)
stage5.stem_cn: 月球居民将能廉价地飞入太空。

stage5.stem: "Mars is ___ to attract many would-be settlers."(‘很可能…’= be __ to do,填那个表‘可能的’形容词)
stage5.stem_cn: 火星很可能吸引许多想移居的人。

stage5.stem: "Mars is 160 times more distant ___ the Moon."(倍数 + 比较级后接的那个连词)
"Mars's biggest chasm is many times ___ than the Grand Canyon."(倍数 + 比较级 + than,填‘宽’那个词的比较级形式)
stage5.stem_cn: 火星最大的裂谷比大峡谷宽好多倍。

stage5.stem: "The Moon's gravity is only a ___ of the Earth's."(分数‘六分之一’,填序数词)
stage5.stem_cn: 月球引力只有地球的六分之一。

stage5.stem: "It ___ much less energy to accelerate on the Moon."(‘做…需要(花费)…’,填 it 后那个动词)
stage5.stem_cn: 在月球上加速所需的能量少得多。

stage5.stem: "It takes less fuel ___ launch a rocket from the Moon."(it takes + 名词 + 不定式,填不定式符号)
stage5.stem_cn: 从月球发射火箭所需燃料更少。

stage5.stem: "It would take enormous energy ___ escape from the Earth."(it takes/would take + 不定式,填不定式符号)
stage5.stem_cn: 要脱离地球引力,得花巨大的能量。

stage5.stem: "Launching from the Moon needs far ___ energy than from Earth."(‘更少的’能量,修饰不可数名词,填 energy 前那个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 从月球发射所需能量远少于从地球。

stage5.stem: "Mars is much ___ distant than the Moon."(‘更远’,distant 的比较级)
"A journey from the Moon costs ___ than one from Earth."(‘更少’,little 的比较级,修饰动词 costs)
stage5.stem_cn: 从月球出发的旅程比从地球出发花费更少。

stage5.stem: "___ escape from the Earth, one must travel at seven miles a second."(不定式作目的状语置于句首,‘为了逃离’,填不定式符号)
stage5.stem_cn: 要脱离地球,须以每秒七英里的速度飞行。

stage5.stem: "Rockets carry lunar fuel ___ reach distant planets."(不定式作目的状语,‘为了到达’,填不定式符号)
stage5.stem_cn: 火箭携带月球燃料,以抵达遥远的行星。

stage5.stem: "Scientists dream of colonies ___ study Mars up close."(不定式作目的状语,‘为了研究’,填不定式符号)
stage5.stem_cn: 科学家梦想建立殖民地,以近距离研究火星。

stage5.stem: "A center of activity around which everything turns is a ___."(“中心,枢纽”用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 一切围之运转的活动中心。

stage5.stem: "A deep crack or opening in a surface is a ___."(“裂口,深渊”用哪个词)
"The word meaning 'relating to the moon' is ___."(“月球的”用哪个词)
